n, k = map(int, input().split())

MAX_SIZE = 33
MOD = 1000000007

class Matrix:
    def __init__(self):
        self.data = [[0]*(MAX_SIZE) for _ in range(MAX_SIZE)]

def multiply_matrices(m1, m2, size):
    result = Matrix()
    for i in range(size+1):
        for j in range(size+1):
            sum_ = 0
            for p in range(size+1):
                sum_ = (sum_ + m1.data[i][p] * m2.data[p][j]) % MOD
            result.data[i][j] = sum_
    return result

# Initialize base_ans
base_ans = Matrix()
for i in range(k+1):
    base_ans.data[i][i] = 1

# Initialize transition matrices
transition = []
for p in range(k):
    mat = Matrix()
    for i in range(k+1):
        for j in range(k+1):
            mat.data[i][j] = 1 if (i == j or i == p) else 0
    transition.append(mat)

# Convert n to base-k digits
digits = []
temp = n
while temp > 0:
    digits.append(temp % k)
    temp //=k
digits.append(0)
# Partial sum in reverse
for i in range(len(digits)-2, -1, -1):
    digits[i] += digits[i+1]

# Process each digit
for p in range(len(digits)-1):
    for i in range(digits[p]-1, digits[p+1]-1, -1):
        base_ans = multiply_matrices(transition[i % k], base_ans, k)
    pre = [None]*k
    suf = [None]*k
    pre[0] = transition[0]
    for i in range(1, k):
        pre[i] = multiply_matrices(pre[i-1], transition[i], k)
    suf[k-1] = transition[k-1]
    for i in range(k-2, -1, -1):
        suf[i] = multiply_matrices(transition[i], suf[i+1], k)
    base_ans = multiply_matrices(suf[0], base_ans, k)
    for i in range(1, k):
        base_ans = multiply_matrices(suf[i], pre[i-1], k)

# Sum over the last row
total = 0
for i in range(k+1):
    total += base_ans.data[i][k]
print(total % MOD)
